What happens to the speed of sound when it travels from air into water?
explanation_english: Sound waves are mechanical vibrations that require a physical medium to propagate, moving faster through denser media with higher bulk modulus. Consequently, the speed of sound increases significantly when transitioning from air into liquid water, rising from about 343 meters per second to roughly 1480 meters per second.

question_english: 19. What is the fundamental working principle behind an electric transformer?

question_english: 95. What process is responsible for converting milk into curd (yogurt)?
